links.outcome: Accuracy and safety (fabrication vs refusal) of LLM answers with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding
links.effect: RAG was the most effective intervention and improved accuracy in complex decision-making tasks. It shifted fabrications to safer refusals but introduced false refusals. Hybrid-RAG was the most robust across tasks.
links.quote: In terms of safety, RAG induced a favorable shift from high-risk fabrications to safer refusals, though this introduced a safety-utility trade-off in the form of false refusals.

unlisted_practices: Domain-specific two-tiered benchmark (MSIC-Bench) for evaluating LLMs in a specialty
Comparing prompting strategies (chain-of-thought, reflection of thoughts) for accuracy and safety

screen.reason: The study empirically tests the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and prompting guardrail/scaffolding strategies against baseline LLM outputs to evaluate impact on accuracy and high-risk fabrications vs. refusals in clinical oncology tasks.
